questions.q: A category B driving licence allows driving a motor vehicle —
options: Up to {{fact:licence.b.max_weight}} and up to {{fact:licence.b.max_passengers}} passengers besides the driver
Up to 12,000 kg only
Of any weight, as long as it has up to 4 passengers
Only a privately owned private car, not a leased one
questions.explain: Regulation 180 defines a B licence as a licence for a motor vehicle whose gross vehicle weight is up to {{fact:licence.b.max_weight}} and up to {{fact:licence.b.max_passengers}} passengers besides the driver.

questions.q: What is required to get a category C driving licence?
options: Age {{fact:licence.c.min_age|n}} and also {{fact:licence.c.seniority_c1}} of seniority in a C1 licence
A B licence only, with no further test
Only a further theory exam, with no age requirement
Only age {{fact:licence.c.min_age|n}}, with no further conditions
questions.explain: Beyond the minimum age, a C licence also requires {{fact:licence.c.seniority_c1}} of seniority in a C1 licence — you cannot skip straight to it.

questions.q: A category 1 driving licence allows driving, among other things —
options: A taxi
A tractor, a mobile machine (except a forklift) and an off-road vehicle
A truck over 12,000 kg
A public minibus
questions.explain: A category 1 licence allows driving a tractor, a mobile machine (other than a forklift, which requires separate conditions), a forklift up to the set weight, an off-road vehicle and an ATV with a permit.

questions.q: A B-licence holder with three or more years of seniority who wants an A2/A1 licence —
options: Cannot get a motorcycle licence at all
Is exempt from the theory exam, and after the required seniority — also exempt from the road-behaviour test
Must wait until age 21
Must sit a full theory exam like any other applicant
questions.explain: A B-licence holder is exempt from the theory exam for a motorcycle licence, and after the required seniority in the B licence is also exempt from the road-behaviour test for an A2/A1 licence.

questions.q: What is required to get a category D (bus) driving licence?
options: No age requirement, only a professional exam
Age {{fact:licence.d.min_age|n}} and also {{fact:licence.d1.seniority_b}} of seniority in a B or C1 licence
A C+E licence only
Only age {{fact:licence.d.min_age|n}}
questions.explain: A D licence requires both a minimum age and seniority in a B or C1 licence, similar to a D1 licence.

questions.q: What is the minimum age for sitting the theory exam for a B licence?
options: {{fact:theory.min_age}}
There is no minimum age for the exam
questions.explain: You can sit the theory exam from age {{fact:theory.min_age|n}}, even before starting actual driving lessons.

questions.q: How many correct answers are needed to pass the theory exam, out of {{fact:theory.questions}} questions?
options: {{fact:theory.pass_correct}} correct answers ({{fact:theory.max_mistakes}} mistakes at most)
Half the questions only
All the questions must be correct
There is no set threshold — it is at the examiner's discretion
questions.explain: You pass the exam with at least {{fact:theory.pass_correct}} correct answers out of {{fact:theory.questions}}, meaning up to {{fact:theory.max_mistakes}} mistakes allowed.

questions.q: What happens if you don't finish all the licensing stages within {{fact:theory.validity}} of the theory exam?
options: You just pay a fine and continue as usual
There is no consequence at all
The exam and test results expire, and you must be tested again
You automatically get a temporary licence
questions.explain: Exam and test results are valid for {{fact:theory.validity}} only; anyone who has not finished within this time has to be tested again.

questions.q: What is the minimum number of driving lessons required for a B licence?
options: {{fact:licence.b.min_lessons}}
There is no fixed minimum in law
questions.explain: A B licence requires at least {{fact:licence.b.min_lessons}} driving lessons with a qualified instructor.

questions.q: You failed the theory exam. Within how long may the licensing authority set a date for a retest?
options: There is no time limit
Only after a year
Within a week only
No later than {{fact:theory.retest_max_wait}}
questions.explain: The licensing authority may set a date for a retest no later than {{fact:theory.retest_max_wait}} from the day of the exam you failed.

questions.q: How long does the "new driver" period last?
options: {{fact:newdriver.duration}} from the day the first licence is received
Until the first accident
Six months only
Until age 21 only
questions.explain: The new-driver period lasts {{fact:newdriver.duration}} from the day the first licence is received, and is extended by a conviction under the Third Schedule.

questions.q: How many escort hours must a young new driver complete, and how are they divided?
options: 10 hours only, with no division
{{fact:newdriver.escort.hours_total}} — {{fact:newdriver.escort.hours_urban}} urban, {{fact:newdriver.escort.hours_nonurban}} non-urban, {{fact:newdriver.escort.hours_night}} night
One hour on every trip for a year
There is no escort duty at all, only a recommendation
questions.explain: Regulation 175B sets at least {{fact:newdriver.escort.hours_total}} of escort: {{fact:newdriver.escort.hours_urban}} urban, {{fact:newdriver.escort.hours_nonurban}} non-urban and {{fact:newdriver.escort.hours_night}} at night.

questions.q: Up to age {{fact:newdriver.passengers.age|n}}, how many passengers may a new driver carry without an accompanying driver (after the escort period)?
options: Only first-degree family members
{{fact:newdriver.passengers.max}} only
No passengers may be carried at all
No limit
questions.explain: Up to age {{fact:newdriver.passengers.age|n}}, a new driver may carry no more than {{fact:newdriver.passengers.max}} passengers without an accompanying driver.

questions.q: Who is exempt from the escort programme for a young new driver?
options: Someone with a senior sibling who has a licence
Someone who completed the IDF's driver mentoring programme and has confirmation of it
Someone who lives near the school
No exemption is possible
questions.explain: Regulation 175D exempts from the escort programme a young new driver who completed the IDF's driver mentoring programme, subject to presenting confirmation from the unit safety officer.

questions.q: Which alcohol threshold applies to a new driver?
options: The stricter threshold — {{fact:alcohol.strict.breath}} in breath
The stricter threshold only in the first year
The ordinary threshold, like any experienced driver
There is no alcohol limit for a new driver
questions.explain: The stricter alcohol threshold — {{fact:alcohol.strict.breath}} — applies to a new driver for the whole new-driver period.

questions.q: What does the vehicle licence certify?
options: That the vehicle is brand new
That the driver has passed the theory exam
That the driver has comprehensive insurance
That the vehicle is registered, has passed the periodic test when required, and the fee has been paid
questions.explain: The vehicle licence certifies the vehicle's registration, that it met the periodic test when required, and that the fee was paid — not the driver's condition.

questions.q: When does a new private vehicle (registered from 1 January 2023) undergo its first periodic test, and how often afterwards?
options: After {{fact:vehicletest.private.first_test_years}} from registration, and then every {{fact:vehicletest.private.interval_years}}
Immediately on registration, and then every year
There is no periodic test for a new private vehicle
Only after 10 years
questions.explain: The first test is {{fact:vehicletest.private.first_test_years}} from the first registration date, and afterwards once every {{fact:vehicletest.private.interval_years}}.

questions.q: What does compulsory insurance cover?
options: Bodily injury to passengers and pedestrians who are hurt, regardless of fault
Property damage to the vehicle itself only
Only damage caused by another driver
Theft of the vehicle only
questions.explain: Compulsory insurance covers bodily injury to those hurt in a road accident — passengers and pedestrians — regardless of who was at fault.

questions.q: A driver is driving with a driving licence that expired three months ago. What is correct?
options: It is allowed, because the licence is still physically in their possession
Only a verbal warning, no fine
No problem, because it expired not long ago
It is an offence — a fine and points, and the longer the time that has passed, the harsher the penalty
questions.explain: Driving with an expired driving licence is an offence; its severity increases the longer the time since it expired.

questions.q: Why is it important to update the licensing authority when you sell a vehicle?
options: Only if the vehicle is sold outside Israel
Otherwise the previous registered owner may be held responsible for the new owner's offences
There is no need — it is the buyer's concern only
To get a refund on the annual fee
questions.explain: Until the records are updated, the owner listed on the licence may be held responsible for offences the new owner commits with the vehicle.

questions.q: What is the authorised doctor's role in getting a driving licence?
options: To examine the practical driving test
To issue a medical certificate for driving, and sometimes set conditions such as a requirement to wear glasses
To train new drivers
Only to collect fees
questions.explain: The authorised doctor examines medical fitness and may issue a medical certificate for driving with conditions and restrictions, such as a requirement for contact lenses or glasses.

questions.q: A driving licence holder discovers a significant change in their vision. What should they do?
options: Wait for the next licence renewal and report it then
There is no duty to report at all, unless asked
Report it immediately by registered letter to the licensing authority
Report it only if the change affects night driving
questions.explain: Regulation 13 requires a driving licence holder who discovers changes in vision (or hearing, the nervous system, or the heart) to report it immediately by registered letter to the licensing authority.

questions.q: A driver drives without the glasses their licence requires, even though they can see well at that moment. What is correct?
options: Allowed only by day, forbidden at night
No offence, because their vision is actually fine
It is a fine offence, because the condition set on the licence was not met
Allowed up to age 30
questions.explain: Driving without the optical aid the licence requires is a fine offence, even if vision appears fine at that moment.

questions.q: From age {{fact:licence.medical.pro_frequent_from_age|n}} and above, how often must a holder of a licence for categories C and above undergo repeat medical checks?
options: No further checks are needed
Once every 10 years
Once only, permanently
Once every {{fact:licence.medical.frequent_every_years}}
questions.explain: A holder of a licence for categories C and above undergoes medical checks once every {{fact:licence.medical.pro_every_years}} from age {{fact:licence.medical.pro_from_age|n}} to {{fact:licence.medical.pro_frequent_from_age|n}}, and from age {{fact:licence.medical.pro_frequent_from_age|n}} — once every {{fact:licence.medical.frequent_every_years}}.

questions.q: Someone who feels wronged by the authorised doctor's decision —
options: Can request a repeat check immediately, with no time limit
Must go to court only
May appeal to an appeals committee within {{fact:licence.medical.appeal_days}} of being notified of the decision
Has no way to appeal at all
questions.explain: Regulation 195 allows an appeal to an appeals committee within {{fact:licence.medical.appeal_days}} of the day the decision was given; the committee can confirm, change, cancel it, or order a repeat examination.
